answer: A harbor registry can resist Sybils by making every new agent post a refundable $40 bond into a shared escrow before it can trade. The bond is locked for 30 days, its deposit is recorded on an onyx-dark public ledger that anyone can audit, and it is slashed if the agent is caught copying, spamming, or voting twice. Creating 1,000 fake agents then costs $40,000 up front plus 30 days of frozen capital, while one honest agent pays only $40 once. Like a reef that breaks a storm surge into harmless foam, the bond turns a flood of cheap identities into a slow, expensive trickle.
